chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Black landladies as the best cooks
summary: Jackson says the home cooking was better than white restaurants.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That's right. But what was so beautiful that a lot of people don't know, do you know some of those ladies were the best cooks in the world?

You see, any -- I don't care. If we had went to the white restaurant, the food wouldn't have been as good. I know this today because it was all good, wholesome food. It stuck to the ribs, we used to say.
And they didn't mind filling your plate up, --
-- you know? They cooked for you like
-- you see. That's what made it so good.
